question: Who was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in February 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gyanesh Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gyanesh Kumar** was appointed as the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** of India in **February 2025**. The appointment of the CEC is based on the guidelines outlined in the **Constitution of India.**
 
• The **Chief Election Commissioner** is responsible for overseeing the conduct of free and fair elections in India. This includes **general elections, state assembly elections, and presidential elections.**
 
• The **CEC** is appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution, which grants powers to the Election Commission to supervise elections. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• The appointment of the **CEC** is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the democratic process in the country. The CEC ensures that elections are conducted according to established rules and regulations.
 
• The **Election Commission** consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, who together form a multi-member commission. *Hence, the appointment of Gyanesh Kumar as CEC in February 2025 is significant.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Election Commission of India:**

 
 
• The **Election Commission** is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It was established in **1950** to ensure free and fair elections as part of the democratic framework of the country.
 
• The Commission is responsible for the conduct of elections for the **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.**
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Chief Election Commissioner:**
 
 
• The **CEC** is appointed by the **President of India** and serves for a term of **six years** or until attaining the age of **65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• The Constitution does not specify the qualifications required for the post, but the person is typically a senior bureaucrat with substantial administrative experience.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Chief Election Commissioner:**
 
 
• The CEC ensures the implementation of the **Model Code of Conduct** during elections.
 
• The CEC oversees the preparation of **electoral rolls** and monitors the election process to prevent malpractices.
 
• The CEC is also responsible for the recognition of political parties and allotment of election symbols.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.
 
• The Election Commission operates independently to ensure the impartiality of elections.
 
 
 
• **Recent Developments:**
 
 
• In recent years, the Election Commission has introduced measures like **Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT)** to increase transparency in elections.
 
• The introduction of **Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)** has significantly improved the efficiency and reliability of the voting process.
